title: A finite type algebra over a field has finitely many isolated spectrum points
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak q\subset A$ for which $\{\mathfrak q\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is finite.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite), proof lines 40362-40420: the finite-type fibre has finitely many isolated points

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to the finite type map $k\to A$ shows that $A$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite), proof lines 40384-40390: the fibre algebra is finite type over the field and hence Noetherian

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], the Noetherian ring $A$ has a finite set of minimal prime ideals.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite), proof lines 40384-40390, using Lemma Tag 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components)

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime whose singleton is open. By the basic-open basis [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], there is $f\in A$ with $\mathfrak q\in D(f)\subseteq\{\mathfrak q\}$, so $D(f)=\{\mathfrak q\}$. If $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ is any prime, then $f\notin\mathfrak q$ implies $f\notin\mathfrak p$, hence $\mathfrak p\in D(f)=\{\mathfrak q\}$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q$. Thus every isolated prime is minimal.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite), proof lines 40362-40368, where isolated points of the finite-type fibre are counted; the minimality argument uses Lemma Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), part (14)

proof.text: The set of isolated primes, including the isolated closed primes counted in the source, is therefore a subset of the finite set of minimal primes from step 2, and is finite.
